subject: Hosted per-token protections and multi-year commit — Clearstream
messages:
From: Diane Morrow <diane.morrow@clearstream.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing protections for hosted per-token usage (initial ask)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — product looked promising. Before we escalate to procurement I need to understand Redwood's stance on price stability for hosted, usage-based contracts. Specifically Clearstream is asking for: 1) a multi-year price lock on the committed per-token rate, 2) an MFN clause (we want parity if Redwood lowers public rates for comparable customers), and 3) a CPI-based cap on annual increases, or alternatively a firm cap (e.g., 0-2%).

Our expected annualized consumption (hosted API) would sit ~1.8B tokens in year 1 with growth into year 2. We prefer a 24-month lock and an MFN that covers pricing for like-for-like commitment and region. Also curious whether Redwood will provide ramp credits if we under-utilize in the first quarter.

Attached: Clearstream_Rate_Protection_Request.pdf (procurement template).

Can you share what you can reasonably offer here? We need to present options to Finance next week.

Best,
Diane
Director, Platform Partnerships
Clearstream Analytics

Attachment: Clearstream_Rate_Protection_Request.pdf (PDF, 124KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diane Morrow <diane.morrow@clearstream.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing protections for hosted per-token usage (initial ask)

Hi Diane — great to hear and glad the demo helped.

High level on what Redwood can do today for hosted, usage-based deals:
- Standard: 12-month price lock on committed per-token rate for the specific model(s) you commit to.
- MFN: not typically standard for hosted offerings, but we can consider a targeted MFN limited to like-for-like commitment tiers and regions rather than unlimited parity.
- CPI Cap: we can add an annual adjustment cap; typical range we've negotiated recently is 0–3% depending on term and commit.
- Ramp credits: yes, we offer limited first-quarter ramp credits for large, front-loaded commitments — amount depends on deal size and expected cadence.

I'm attaching a draft term sheet with an initial economic proposal (Redwood_Initial_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf). If you can share the procurement constraints (e.g., legal MFN language or a required CPI formula) it will help accelerate a response.

Would you be open to an 18-month price lock as a starting point? That tends to be an easier middle ground. Happy to jump on a call with Procurement this week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Initial_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf (PDF, 98KB)

From: Diane Morrow <diane.morrow@clearstream.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@clearstream.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing protections for hosted per-token usage (initial ask)

Thanks Marissa — received the term sheet. A few follow-ups from Procurement and Finance:

- We really prefer a 24-month lock; 18 months is a step in the right direction but Finance is pushing for 24.
- MFN: procurement wants a general MFN for any publicly-available per-token price reductions for hosted API customers with comparable commitment and region; they understand carve-outs for promotional/one-off offers but want standard parity otherwise.
- CPI: finance asked if Redwood would accept a 0% CPI cap for the committed per-token rate (i.e., no annual increases for the duration of the lock). If not, a 1% max would be acceptable.
- Ramp credits: we are asking for a partial credit equal to 10% of the committed spend if we miss the first-quarter ramp by >30%.

Attached: procurement_form_clearstream.pdf (procurement team standard).

Diane

Attachment: procurement_form_clearstream.pdf (PDF, 82KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Clearstream pricing protections — need legal/econ guidance

Team — forwarding procurement asks from Clearstream (see attachment). Key asks: 24-month lock, broad MFN for hosted per-token pricing, 0–1% CPI cap, and 10% ramp-credit. Need quick guidance on what we can reasonably concede without opening the door to broad MFNs.

Suggested play: offer 18–20 month lock with a 2% CPI cap, MFN but limited to customers with same commit size (+/-20%) and same region, and structured ramp credit (sliding scale up to 8%). Also propose an escrow/notification clause for public price drops so we avoid perpetual MFN exposure.

What are the legal redline risks here (MFN language specifically)? If we can get to an 18–20 month lock we should be able to hit revenue targets while protecting pricing flexibility.

Thanks —
Marissa
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Clearstream_Rate_Protection_Request.pdf (PDF, 124KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clearstream pricing protections — need legal/econ guidance

Marissa — quick thoughts from Legal + Pricing:

- MFN: legal flags broad MFNs as high-risk (can cascade and restrict ability to run targeted promos). Recommend a scoped MFN: parity only to published "standard rates" for hosted per-token where a customer has the same committed annualized token volume (±20%) and commits to the same model family and region. Add a 30-day notice and cure period.
- Price lock: we can stretch to 20 months with minimal margin impact if we require upfront payment of at least 40% of year-1 committed spend and annual true-up.
- CPI cap: recommend 2% cap; 0% is hard for multi-year due to infrastructure cost inflation.
- Ramp credit: accept up to 8% of committed spend as a sliding credit if clear ramp milestones are missed; ties to documented usage metrics.

I've attached a proposed redline with suggested legal language for the MFN and escrow/notification flow: redline_proposal_20261015.docx. If Sales is comfortable with the upfront payment requirement, we can present this as the commercial compromise.

Karthik
Head of Pricing & Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redline_proposal_20261015.docx (DOCX, 56KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diane Morrow <diane.morrow@clearstream.ai>, Procurement <procurement@clearstream.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing protections for hosted per-token usage — Redwood counteroffer

Hi Diane — thanks for the clear asks and for sharing the procurement form. We've worked through this internally and here is the counteroffer we can present to Clearstream: 

1) Price lock: 20-month lock on the committed per-token rate for the specific model family you select.
2) MFN: scoped MFN limited to public, published hosted per-token rates for customers with the same committed annualized token volume (±20%), same model family, and same region. MFN excludes time-limited promotional discounts and partner-reseller pricing. Includes 30-day notice and 60-day cure window.
3) CPI cap: 2% annual cap on increases to the committed per-token rate during the lock period.
4) Ramp credits: sliding ramp credit up to 8% of year-1 committed spend if documented usage/ramp milestones are missed by more than 30% in Q1.
5) Upfront: require 40% upfront payment of year-1 committed spend to secure the extended lock term. Annual true-up at year end.
6) SLA & credits: 99.95% uptime SLA for dedicated infra paths; hosted service SLA credits available for sustained outages as defined in the term sheet.

Next steps: we've attached the redlined term sheet reflecting the above (Redwood_Final_Term_Sheet_CLEAR-2026-07.pdf). If this aligns with Clearstream's constraints we can route to DocuSign and put Procurement + Legal on a 30-minute review call this week.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

Would you like a short call tomorrow to walk through the MFN language?

Best regards,
